exercise.name: Hamstring Bridge

reference.title: Hamstring Bridge (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip extension with the knees only slightly bent)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you dig the heels in and lift, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, 1 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.progression: Feet further out, then single-leg hamstring bridge, then heels on a bench

cues.text: Lie on your back with the heels on the mat well past the knees, toes pulled up, knees slightly bent, arms by your sides.
Breathe out, dig the heels into the floor and lift the hips.
Shoulders, hips and knees in one line; feel the backs of the thighs work.
Breathe in and lower the hips slowly to the mat.

mistakes.fix: Toes up, drive through the heels only.
Ribs down, slight pelvic tuck before you lift.

mistakes.mistake: Feet too close (becomes a glute bridge)
mistakes.fix: Keep the heels well past the knees so the knees stay only slightly bent.
Shorten the lever (feet a little closer) and build up.

kinematics.norm: Hips extend to about neutral at the top (clinical opinion)
Knees only slightly to moderately bent (about 30-50 degrees); less knee bend raises hamstring activity in bridging (Lehecka 2017)
Toes pulled up, weight on the heels (clinical opinion)
Pelvis lifts until shoulders, hips and knees line up (clinical opinion)
About 1.5 s up, a 1 s squeeze, 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Hamstring cramps: lower, rest and bring the feet a little closer.
Low back discomfort: lift less high and brace first.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Main target: with the knees nearly straight the hamstrings do most of the hip extension (Lehecka 2017 found more hamstring activity with less knee bend).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Main target: with the knees nearly straight the hamstrings do most of the hip extension (Lehecka 2017 found more hamstring activity with less knee bend).
